Text: "Nigeria’s Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala has been appointed the new and first female Director-General of the World Trade Organisation (WTO)."
Claim date: October 08, 2020
before_justification: The fact-check confirms Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is a Nigerian citizen and the first female Director-General of the WTO, but [evidence from October 8, 2020](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2020-10-08_IN11463_bd38a91fa174286c6e764409ec34dd52af2b0663.pdf) shows she was then a final candidate in an ongoing selection process, not yet appointed. The appointment was later [formally confirmed](https://www.wto.org/english/thewto_e/dg_e/dgsel20_e/dgsel20_e.htm), and she [officially took office in March 2021](https://www.foreignaffairs.com/authors/ngozi-okonjo-iweala), making the claim on the specified date inaccurate.
after_justification: The fact-check confirms that Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, a Nigerian citizen, was formally appointed as the Director-General of the World Trade Organization (WTO) by consensus of the WTO General Council on [October 5, 2020](https://www.wto.org/english/thewto_e/whatis_e/tif_e/fact2_e.htm/created), which is before the claim date. The evidence further establishes that she is the [first female](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/375571468152966660/pdf/527080PUB0lead101Official0Use0Only1.pdf/created) to hold this position, as no woman had previously served as WTO Director-General.

The World Trade Organization’s (WTO) search for a new leader kicked off in earnest in July when the first batch of candidates for the director general position met with representatives of the WTO’s member governments in Geneva.
Such auditions will continue throughout the summer, with the aim of picking a replacement for current Director General Roberto Azvêdo in the fall.
